subject: future
topic: Is there a limit to how long humans can live?
angle: While there is a high probability that the current maximum human lifespan will be broken by 2100, the extent of this extension is governed by quantitative rules of hormesis and potential senotherapeutic interventions.
title: The end of the limit

hooks.text: Is there a limit to how long you can live?
You think 122 is the limit. The evidence suggests otherwise.
You are accepting a biological ceiling you didn't choose.
A flickering screen in a dark room.
A 99% probability of breaking the record.

reveal.headline: The current human age limit will likely break.
reveal.body: There is a greater than 99% probability that the current maximum reported age at death of 122 will be broken by 2100. The evidence is mixed.

explain.headline: Biology follows quantitative rules.
explain.body: Hormesis defines the rules for how biological performance and lifespan can be enhanced. Natural products like fisetin show senotherapeutic activity in mice and human tissues.

matters.headline: Your lifespan is a variable.
matters.body: That may be why your aging is being viewed as a biological process that can be adjusted through specific interventions rather than a fixed end point.

example.headline: A glass of water on a nightstand.
example.body: You watch the light change on the wall as you prepare for sleep, unaware of the chemical processes governing your cells tonight.

question.headline: How long do you intend to stay?

verdict: The evidence suggests that human lifespan is not currently capped at 122 and may be extendable through biological and pharmacological interventions.
caveat: The probability of reaching extreme ages like 130 remains relatively low at 13% according to current Bayesian projections.
caption:
The human lifespan may not have a fixed ceiling.

Research suggests a greater than 99% probability that the current record of 122 will be broken by 2100.

What does it mean for you if aging becomes a manageable variable?
